absent: Internal behavior of nested offset merge, permission map allocation, AVIC setup, PMU capability init, MSR list init and MMU vendor hooks is absent.
Exact encodings, widths and side effects of TSC ratio, TSC AUX, EFER, PAT, CET, XSS and SEV related registers beyond enablement checks is absent.
Detailed layouts of virtual CPU, virtual machine, x86 ops, nested ops, PMU ops and VP assist structures beyond referenced fields is absent.
Concurrency and locking for per CPU bringup, posted interrupts, timers, workqueues and perf callbacks beyond vendor module mutex is absent.
Guest visible semantics, fault delivery and performance implications of MMIO masks, NPT levels and capability bits is absent.
Failure handling inside SEV, Hyper-V enlightened flush and CPU compatibility callbacks is absent.

findings.text: kvm_x86_vendor_init provides global x86 vendor bringup that consumes an init operations bundle and returns a status code, establishing capabilities, emulator resources, memory management hooks, hardware setup, operation vectors, compatibility checks and timer and performance integrations.

kvm_x86_vendor_exit provides global x86 vendor teardown that releases performance callbacks, local APIC state, clock and paravirtual clock integrations, hardware setup, user return MSRs, memory management vendor state and emulator cache, and clears the virtualization enable hook under lock.

kvm_init provides generic virtualization bringup parameterized by virtual CPU object size and alignment plus owner module, creating caches and subsystems and exposing the control device only as the final step.

Perf callback registration stores optional handlers for Intel processor trace interrupts and mediated performance interrupts then registers a guest callback bundle, while unregistration removes that bundle.

IRQ file descriptor and asynchronous page fault subsystems each expose paired init and exit operations for global setup and teardown, with IRQ setup provisioning a dedicated cleanup workqueue and async setup provisioning a dedicated object cache.

kvm_setup_xss_caps adjusts advertised extended supervisor state capabilities based on presence of save supervisor and control flow features, enforcing all or nothing treatment for shadow stack and indirect branch tracking.

SVM Hyper-V integration exposes a hardware setup hook that enables enlightened flush operations when nested features advertise them, with an empty fallback variant when that integration is unavailable.

Vendor bringup refuses to proceed when another vendor is already active, when floating point or fast save restore support is missing, when realtime operation lacks an invariant timestamp counter, when host page attribute entry zero does not encode write back, or when supervisor shadow stack appears unexpectedly enabled, reporting distinct failure statuses for each case.

SVM hardware setup requires non execute support and otherwise degrades optional controls gracefully, disabling timestamp scaling, pause filtering thresholds, nested paging, guest metadata, next RIP save, lightweight virtualization aids, virtual GIF and virtual NMI when host capabilities or configuration do not allow them.

SVM advertises a fixed maximum scaling ratio and a fractional width of thirty two bits, while generic bringup derives a default ratio of one shifted by that width and bounds the maximum guest frequency using the host frequency and the maximum ratio.

Memory mapped input output fault mask selection leaves any existing mask unchanged when extended CPU identification or memory encryption enablement is absent, otherwise it chooses a mask bit derived from host physical width adjusted away from the encryption position, using reserved plus present semantics below a threshold and clearing the mask at or above it.

SVM capability construction starts from generic initialization, advertises nested virtualization features only when nesting is enabled, refines virtualization of secure boot, performance counters and encryption features, clears bus lock detection and immediate moves that lack explicit support, then applies extended state handling and finalization.

Extended supervisor state support is cleared entirely when save supervisor is unavailable, and control flow protection state is kept only when both shadow stack and indirect branch tracking remain available, otherwise both features and their state bits are removed together.

Advertised extended feature enable bits always include system call extension, with long mode, no execute, fast FXSAVE restore optimization, automatic branch protection and virtualization controls added only when corresponding processor features are present, including a model specific guard for a legacy segmentation bit.

Nested paging is forced off without host support or without a paging mode that the memory management unit can use, and when enabled it drives memory management configuration to match host paging levels with a one gigabyte ceiling while disabling support for guests with smaller physical width than the host.

When accelerated interrupt virtualization is unavailable the implementation nullifies a group of related callbacks for precreation, destruction, blocking and inhibition reporting, and when virtual NMI is unavailable it nullifies pending state accessors.

The x86 emulation cache is created as an accounted slab object sized and aligned for the emulation context, with a user copy region that starts at the source operand area and extends to the end of the object.

Virtual machine object sizes are constrained at build time so that their allocation order remains small unless debugging aids are enabled, applied to the SVM specific virtual machine container during module initialization.

Generic bringup seeds supported quirks and conditional quirks, removes a code segment quirk for SVM, drops guest page attribute ignoring when two dimensional paging is off, and enables a software protected virtual machine type only when protected memory and two dimensional memory management are both active.
When secure encrypted virtualization support is compiled out, its CPU capability and hardware setup hooks are defined as empty operations that leave state unchanged.

Access to the global vendor operation vector during load and unload is serialized by a dedicated vendor module mutex, acquired automatically for the whole duration of vendor initialization and explicitly around clearing of the virtualization enable hook during vendor exit.

The SVM initialization bundle aggregates four references covering hardware setup, runtime operation vector, performance operation vector and nested operation vector, consumed once during vendor bringup.

Runtime operation vectors are installed by copying the supplied table into global state and then refreshing dispatched call sites, distinguishing required entries that warn when absent from optional entries and from optional entries that safely return zero.

Nested operation vectors are installed by copying the supplied table into global state and then refreshing dispatched call sites, distinguishing required entries that warn when absent from optional entries and from optional entries that safely return zero.

SVM module initialization validates object size, confirms processor support, delegates to generic vendor bringup and only then exposes generic services, unwinding through vendor exit if generic bringup fails.

Vendor bringup proceeds through validation, resource creation, vendor hardware setup, feature finalization, operation installation and per processor compatibility verification, after which timer and notification integrations are installed and further failures are treated as exceptional rather than following normal unwind.

Generic bringup creates virtual CPU cache, per processor kick masks, interrupt file descriptor and async fault services, assigns module ownership, installs scheduling hooks, initializes debugging, virtualization IO and guest memory services, enables virtualization and finally registers the control device, unwinding in reverse order on any failure.

SVM hardware setup orders timestamp and pause controls before nesting enablement, paging and memory encryption configuration before permission maps and encryption hardware, and accelerated interrupt and virtualization aid tuning before capability finalization and per processor initialization.
SVM module entry validates environment and chains vendor specific and generic bringup so that user visible device creation happens last.
SVM hardware setup acts as the vendor callback invoked once during generic vendor bringup to configure paging, interrupts, counters and capabilities before per processor activation.

Clock tracking initialization takes effect only on systems without an invariant timestamp counter, where it derives a maximum frequency from firmware or power management data and installs frequency change and hotplug integrations.

Resource exhaustion during cache, mask, permission map or emulator allocation fails bringup with out of memory and releases already acquired resources, while per processor activation failure triggers a full hardware teardown.
Hyper-V direct flush enablement tolerates missing per processor assist pages by skipping those processors while still installing the level two flush hook.
Vendor exit must synchronize interrupt work and cancel pending timekeeping work before invoking hardware teardown and destroying shared caches, otherwise teardown could race with in flight callbacks.
Timestamp scaling fractional width is 32 bits.
Host page attribute entry zero is required to encode write back with low three bits equal to 6.
Memory mapped input output mask generation treats 52 as the threshold and 51 as the upper reserved bound.
Encryption mask logic keys on CPUID leaves 0x80000000 and 0x8000001f and on the memory encryption enable indication in MSR_AMD64_SYSCFG.
